plan: Nine new items (two words-in-context with uncommon distractors, a cause-isolating data item, inference, concession transition, an explain-how synthesis, since + present perfect, each-of agreement, central idea); S016-03 resubmitted relabelled easy with a face-only fix.

passages.title: The negotiator
passages.text: Observers described the negotiator's manner as ______: although she firmly rejected each of the union's demands, she did so with such courtesy and tact that the meeting ended in handshakes.

passages.title: A quiet mayor
passages.text: Unlike his ______ predecessor, who held a press conference to announce even the most minor decisions and seemed never to tire of speaking to reporters, the new mayor rarely gave interviews.

passages.title: Library hours
passages.text:
After a public library began staying open until 9:00 p.m. on weekdays, a researcher compared its average monthly visits before and after the change.
Time period | Before | After
Weekday mornings | 120 | 118
Weekday evenings | 60 | 145
Weekends | 200 | 210
The researcher claims that the extended evening hours, rather than a general rise in interest in the library, account for most of the increase in visits.

passages.title: Fig wasps
passages.text: Some species of fig tree are pollinated by only a single species of tiny wasp, and that wasp can reproduce only inside the figs of that tree species. Because of this close dependence, a sharp decline in the wasp population would most likely ______

passages.title: A growing main street
passages.text: The town's population fell by about a third between 1990 and 2010. ______ the number of businesses on its main street nearly doubled over the same period, as tourists began visiting its restored historic district.

passages.title: Ancient gears
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Antikythera mechanism is an ancient Greek device recovered from a shipwreck in 1901.
• It contains at least 30 interlocking bronze gears.
• Turning a hand crank moved the gears, which advanced pointers on dials.
• The pointers showed the positions of the Sun and Moon in the sky.

passages.title: A museum collection
passages.text: Since 2015, the city's history museum ______ more than forty paintings by local artists, many of them donated by the artists' families.

passages.title: Twelve paintings
passages.text: The gallery's most popular room displays a cycle of twelve paintings by a seventeenth-century Flemish artist. Each of the twelve paintings ______ a different month of the year through the work done in the fields at that time.

passages.title: Solar siblings
passages.text: Most stars form in clusters from the same cloud of gas, but over hundreds of millions of years the members of a cluster drift apart. Astronomers comparing the chemical makeup of nearby stars with that of the Sun have identified a few whose compositions are nearly identical to the Sun's, which suggests that they formed in the same cloud. Studying these "solar siblings" could help researchers reconstruct the environment in which the Sun was born.

passages.title: Sheep and faces
passages.text: An animal behaviorist hypothesizes that sheep identify familiar people mainly by their faces rather than by other cues, such as voice, clothing, or smell.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
candidates.evidence: she did so with such courtesy and tact
candidates.explanation: Firm on substance but courteous and tactful in manner: "diplomatic."

A.rationale: "Obsequious" means overly eager to please, but she firmly rejected every demand.

B.rationale: "Brusque" means curt or rude, the opposite of courteous and tactful.

D.rationale: "Equivocal" means ambiguous, but her rejections were firm and clear.

hints: The text describes both firmness and courtesy. Which word captures both?
candidates.remember: Choose the word that fits every detail in the context.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
candidates.evidence: seemed never to tire of speaking to reporters
candidates.explanation: The predecessor constantly spoke to reporters: "loquacious," meaning very talkative. "Unlike" contrasts him with the reserved new mayor.

B.rationale: "Reticent" describes the new mayor, not the predecessor; "Unlike" signals the opposite.

C.rationale: "Magnanimous" means generous and forgiving, which the text does not address.

D.rationale: "Capricious" means unpredictable; the predecessor was consistently talkative.

hints: Which person does the blank describe, the predecessor or the new mayor?
candidates.remember: Track which person a blank describes after "unlike."

candidates.subskill: Command of evidence: quantitative (isolating a cause)
candidates.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the researcher's claim?

choices.A: Total average monthly visits rose from 380 before the change to 473 after it, an increase of 93.
choices.B: Evening visits rose by 85, while weekday-morning visits fell slightly and weekend visits rose by only 10.
choices.C: Weekends remained the busiest of the three time periods both before and after the change in hours.
choices.D: Weekday-morning visits fell slightly, from an average of 120 a month to an average of 118 a month.

candidates.evidence: account for most of the increase in visits
candidates.explanation: The claim separates the evening increase from general interest. Evenings rose by 85 while the other periods barely changed, so most of the increase came from the new hours.

A.rationale: This shows an increase but not that it came mainly from the evening hours.

C.rationale: This does not address where the increase came from.

D.rationale: A small drop in mornings alone does not show that evenings drove the increase.

hints: What would a general rise in interest look like in the table?
candidates.remember: To isolate a cause, compare the changed condition with the unchanged ones.

candidates.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: lead other wasp species to begin pollinating the fig trees.
choices.B: increase the number of figs the trees produce each year.
choices.C: have no effect on the trees, whose figs need no pollination.
choices.D: reduce the fig trees' ability to produce seeds.

candidates.evidence: are pollinated by only a single species of tiny wasp
candidates.explanation: If only one wasp species pollinates the trees, fewer wasps means less pollination, so fewer seeds.

A.rationale: Only a single wasp species pollinates these trees.

B.rationale: Fewer pollinators would not increase fruit production.

C.rationale: The text says the trees depend on the wasp for pollination.

hints: What do the trees need from the wasp?

strategy.explanation: Eliminate choices that contradict the dependence.

candidates.remember: Exclusive dependence: losing one partner harms the other.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
candidates.evidence: nearly doubled over the same period
candidates.explanation: Despite the population decline, businesses increased: an unexpected contrast, so "Even so."

A.rationale: A shrinking population did not cause businesses to multiply.

B.rationale: The rise in businesses is not an example of population decline.

D.rationale: The two trends move in opposite directions; they are not alike.

hints: Do the two trends go in the same direction?
candidates.remember: Concession transitions introduce a result that defies expectation.

candidates.stem: The student wants to explain how the Antikythera mechanism operated. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Its hand crank turned bronze gears that advanced pointers showing the Sun's and Moon's positions.
choices.B: The Antikythera mechanism, an ancient Greek device, was recovered by divers from a sunken shipwreck in 1901.
choices.C: The Antikythera mechanism contains at least 30 bronze gears, all of which interlock with one another.
choices.D: The pointers on the Antikythera mechanism's dials showed where the Sun and Moon appeared in the sky.

candidates.evidence: Turning a hand crank moved the gears, which advanced pointers on dials.
candidates.explanation: Explaining operation requires the sequence from input to output: crank, gears, pointers, positions. Only A gives it.

B.rationale: This tells when and where it was found, not how it worked.

C.rationale: This lists a part but does not explain how the parts produced a result.

D.rationale: This gives the output but not the mechanism that produced it.

hints: What does a description of how something works need to include?

strategy.explanation: Name the goal, then check each choice.

candidates.remember: "How it worked" means the chain from input to output.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
candidates.explanation: "Since 2015" marks a period from the past up to now, so the present perfect "has acquired" is needed.

A.rationale: "Since 2015" describes a period continuing to the present, which calls for the present perfect, not the simple past.

B.rationale: The simple present does not fit an accumulation over a period beginning in the past.

hints: Does "since 2015" describe a finished time or one continuing to now?
candidates.remember: "Since" + a past starting point usually takes the present perfect.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
candidates.explanation: The subject is "Each," which is singular, so the verb is "depicts."

A.rationale: "Each" is singular, so the verb must be singular; "paintings" is part of a prepositional phrase.

C.rationale: "Are" is plural and does not agree with "Each."

D.rationale: "Have" is plural, and the present perfect does not fit a description of the paintings.

hints: What is the simple subject: "Each" or "paintings"?
candidates.remember: "Each of the ___" takes a singular verb.

candidates.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Most stars remain close to the other members of their original cluster for the whole of their lives.
choices.B: The Sun's chemical makeup is unusual compared with that of nearly all the other stars in the galaxy.
choices.C: Astronomers have now fully reconstructed the cloud of gas in which the Sun originally formed.
choices.D: Stars whose makeup matches the Sun's may have formed alongside it and could reveal clues to its birth.

candidates.evidence: could help researchers reconstruct the environment in which the Sun was born
candidates.explanation: The text explains that cluster stars drift apart, that some nearby stars match the Sun's makeup, and that they may reveal its birth environment.

A.rationale: The text says cluster members drift apart.

B.rationale: The text says some stars share its makeup; it does not call the Sun unusual.

C.rationale: The text says studying siblings "could help"; the work is not finished.

hints: What do the matching stars suggest, and why does it matter?

strategy.explanation: Eliminate choices that contradict or overstate.

candidates.subskill: Command of evidence: textual (supporting a hypothesis)
candidates.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the behaviorist's hypothesis?

choices.A: Sheep trained to approach a familiar handler chose photographs showing only that handler's face over photographs of strangers' faces.
choices.B: Sheep approached a familiar handler more readily when the handler wore the same jacket as during earlier visits than when the handler wore a new one.
choices.C: Sheep in large flocks were found to respond to familiar handlers' voices more quickly than sheep in small flocks responded to those voices.
choices.D: Sheep kept near people for several years approached any human more readily than sheep that had little contact with people did.

candidates.evidence: identify familiar people mainly by their faces
candidates.explanation: Choosing a familiar person's face-only photograph, with voice, clothing and smell all absent, isolates faces as the cue and directly supports the hypothesis.

B.rationale: This suggests clothing matters, which the hypothesis says is not the main cue.

C.rationale: This concerns voice, not faces, and compares flock sizes.

D.rationale: Approaching any human does not show recognition of familiar individuals by face.

hints: Which finding rules out the other cues the hypothesis names?

strategy.explanation: Eliminate findings that point to other cues.

candidates.remember: Support for a hypothesis isolates the proposed cause.
candidates.revision_note: S016-03 resubmitted relabelled easy (both solvers about 72%), with choice A changed to face-only photographs because both solvers noted that a full photograph could also show clothing.
